absent: Numeric values and bit layout of affinity selectors, dequeue options, task states, wait flags and error codes.
Lock ordering, interrupt state and sleeping rules for runqueue versus pi protection beyond paired acquire and release shown.
Behavior of placement, clock, tracing, scheduling, preemption and reference counting helpers referenced but not routed.
Stop work scheduling guarantees, completion signaling and variable wait queue sizing and hashing details beyond call sites.
Destination processor choice policy, load effects and hotplug interaction for failed or retried moves.
Memory management propagation effects and identifier threshold derivation beyond observed monotonic growth sketch.
State predicate encoding for inactive wait matching, including saved state representation and switch count width.

findings.text: Scheduler exposes a blocking waiter that reports when a chosen thread is neither executing on a processor nor present on scheduling queues for a caller supplied state predicate, returning a marked switch count on match and zero on mismatch.

Scheduler exposes affinity update entries that accept a thread plus a mask context and funnel plain, user aware, checked and migrate mode requests through a common locked installer that validates, stores and possibly relocates the thread.

Scheduler exposes migration pinning wrappers that delegate disable and enable transitions to inner helpers, with a switch helper that pins the effective mask to the current processor only while pinning is active and a restore helper that points back at the durable mask.

Wait machinery exposes variable based wakeup plus bit keyed and queue based wakeup that resolve a shared queue from an address hash and iterate registered waiters under protection while honoring exclusive consumption.
Scheduler exposes duplication of a caller supplied restriction mask across thread creation with guarded copy and allocation failure reporting, plus clearing and freeing helpers for teardown.

Scheduler exposes a common mask store that either redirects the effective pointer for transient migrate modes or copies the durable mask, refreshes the allowed count, notifies memory management and optionally exchanges the user restriction, plus a locked helper that transfers a queued thread between queues.

Migration stopper entry runs on a target processor to finalize affinity moves, handling same queue versus moved queue cases, short circuiting disabled migration, completing shared pending state and requeuing stop work when the target moved away.

Push stopper entry runs to move an over constrained thread toward a more suitable queue, deferring with a push marker when migration is disabled, otherwise locating and switching to a destination queue then requesting rescheduling there.
Migration argument bundle associates a thread reference with a destination processor identifier and a link to shared pending state used for completion signaling.
Shared affinity pending record combines lifetime counting with a marker for queued stop work, a completion signal, stop work storage and embedded migration arguments.

Inactive wait progresses through optimistic unsynchronized spinning while on processor, then locked sampling of running and queued indicators plus state match, then either mismatch exit or running retry or timed sleep while queued or success when neither running nor queued.

Affinity relocation first succeeds immediately when the current processor remains allowed or a donor exception applies, otherwise installs or joins shared pending state, then for executing or waking threads queues stop work a single time while for other threads performs direct queue transfer when permitted, finishing with completion and a reference barrier.
Wake scan walks queue entries in order and invokes each waiter callback, stopping early on negative result and consuming exclusive allowance only on positive results from exclusive waiters.
Wait path forces removal of delayed schedulable state before sampling and treats a saved state match as if queued so the caller continues waiting, marking the returned count with a high bit on match.

Locked affinity installer widens the valid set for kernel threads and disabled migration, rejects plain masks outside the possible set and checked threads marked no affinity, treats equal masks as success with optional user exchange, rejects a pinned current thread leaving its processor, and fails when no destination intersection exists.

Outer affinity entry intersects the requested mask with the stored user restriction unless user or migrate control modes are indicated, redirecting the effective request to scratch storage on success.

Restrictive affinity update refuses deadline constrained threads when bandwidth control is active and refuses empty intersections between stored user allowance and supplied subset before delegating to the locked installer.

Memory identifier allowance update grows monotonically with early exits for absent management or unchanged weight, recomputing limits and thresholds and deferring wider propagation through queued work only when conditions favor a return toward per processor mode, with an alternate build that performs no action.

Queued transfer removes the thread from its old queue, retargets its processor association, switches queue locks, then inserts into the new queue and evaluates preemption, asserting lock ownership and destination consistency and skipping moves to disallowed destinations in the guarded variant.
Pinned task presence on a queue is reported from a per queue counter.
Variable wait queues are selected by hashing the variable address into a shared table and waking through the resulting head.

Affinity and migration paths acquire runqueue and thread pi protection together through task queue locking, release both together on completion paths, and transfer runqueue ownership when switching queues during direct moves, with the stopper additionally stabilizing interrupt state and aliasing context across the switch.

Queue wakeup serializes the waiter walk with interrupt saving spin protection around the common iteration, which asserts that protection is held and returns remaining exclusive allowance to the caller.

User restriction mask content is guarded by pi protection during duplication copy, with an initial unsynchronized presence check treated as racy but benign and with allocation sized to cover both mask storage and deferred release header.

Push path holds pi and source queue protection, optionally acquires a second queue, then releases the pair with balanced handling for same versus distinct queue identities and clears busy indication under source protection before dropping references.

Migrate disable switch applies mask fixation under scoped task queue guard only when pinning is active and the effective pointer still references the durable mask, anchored to the current queue processor.

Inactive waiter reads queue association without locks during optimistic spinning and tolerates queue identity change, relying on later locked sampling to correct, with busy spinning while executing and timed uninterruptible sleep while queued.

Concurrent affinity requests share a single pending record with reference counting plus completion broadcast and a variable address wakeup plus a barrier that holds the original installer until later joiners release, warning if stop indication remains at the end.

Migration stopper chases the thread to its new processor when queue mismatch shows disallowed placement, requeuing stop work and returning without completion, and may leave execution on an unexpected processor during hot removal scenarios.

Affinity fast and stop paths disable preemption across queue release and stop queueing to stabilize processor association, reenabling immediately after, while the stopper flushes pending cross processor work before sampling placement.

One build variant defines cross processor queue flushing as an empty inline, so stopper ordering guarantees that depend on it differ by configuration, and memory identifier updates are likewise configuration dependent.
Affinity control uses selector names SCA_USER and SCA_CHECK plus SCA_MIGRATE_DISABLE and SCA_MIGRATE_ENABLE.
Dequeue handling uses names DEQUEUE_SLEEP and DEQUEUE_DELAYED plus DEQUEUE_NOCLOCK, and pinned deferral uses MDF_PUSH.
Affinity validation reports names EINVAL and EBUSY plus EPERM and ENOMEM, and consults thread flags PF_KTHREAD and PF_NO_SETAFFINITY.
Wait and wake handling uses TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE and TASK_WAKING plus TASK_NORMAL and WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE.
